question: Co-operative societies are primarily accountable to which of the following? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Local Municipal Body
Co-operative Society Members
Central Government
Reserve Bank of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Co-operative Society Members

Explanation:
Co-operative societies are voluntary organizations formed by their members, operating on the principle of mutual assistance. They are primarily accountable to their members because members are both the owners and operators of the society. According to the Co-operative Societies Act, societies must fulfill the needs of their members and remain transparent towards them. External bodies like the local municipal corporation, central government, or RBI do not directly interfere in their daily activities. The democratic control by members ensures that the society works for their welfare.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Primary objective of co-operative society → Promotion of cooperative activities for members' welfare
☛ Regulation of co-operative societies → Under the Co-operative Societies Act, 1904 (since amended)
☛ Relationship with other bodies → RBI regulates only co-operative banks, not all societies
☛ Democratic principle → One member, one vote
☛ Profit distribution → A part of profit is distributed as dividend among members
question_hi: सहकारी समितियाँ मुख्य रूप से निम्नलिखित में से किसके प्रति उत्तरदायी होती हैं? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: स्थानीय नगरपालिका निकाय
सहकारी समिति के सदस्य
केंद्रीय सरकार
भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सहकारी समिति के सदस्य

Explanation:
सहकारी समितियाँ अपने सदस्यों द्वारा स्वैच्छिक रूप से बनाई गई संस्थाएँ होती हैं, जो आपसी सहयोग के सिद्धांत पर काम करती हैं। ये मुख्य रूप से अपने सदस्यों के प्रति उत्तरदायी होती हैं क्योंकि सदस्य ही समिति के मालिक और संचालक होते हैं। सहकारिता अधिनियम के अनुसार, समितियों को सदस्यों की जरूरतों को पूरा करना होता है और उनके प्रति पारदर्शी रहना होता है। स्थानीय नगरपालिका, केंद्र सरकार या RBI जैसी बाहरी संस्थाएँ इनकी दैनिक गतिविधियों में सीधा हस्तक्षेप नहीं करतीं।

question: Under what circumstance can the President of India dissolve the Lok Sabha before its normal term expires? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: On the recommendation of the Prime Minister
Whenever the President wishes, without any conditions
After consulting a joint session of both Houses of Parliament
When the Supreme Court orders a dissolution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is On the recommendation of the Prime Minister

Explanation:
According to Article 85(2)(b) of the Constitution of India, the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha before its normal term expires, but this power is exercised only on the recommendation of the Prime Minister. This is based on the advice of the Council of Ministers, which is binding on the President. The President cannot dissolve the Lok Sabha arbitrarily or on the order of the Supreme Court. Consultation with a joint session of Parliament is not mandatory. This provision is an integral part of the parliamentary system, where the President is the nominal head and real power rests with the Prime Minister. If the Prime Minister loses a vote of confidence and no alternative government is formed, dissolution occurs only upon recommendation.

☛ Which Article of the Constitution deals with dissolution of Lok Sabha? → Article 85(2)(b)
☛ Can the President dissolve Lok Sabha at his own will? → No, only on the advice of the Council of Ministers
☛ Who is the head of the Council of Ministers? → Prime Minister
☛ What type of government system does India have? → Parliamentary system
question_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति किस परिस्थिति में लोकसभा को उसके सामान्य कार्यकाल की समाप्ति से पहले भंग कर सकते हैं? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: प्रधानमंत्री की अनुशंसा पर
जब भी राष्ट्रपति चाहें, बिना किसी शर्त के
संसद के दोनों सदनों के संयुक्त सत्र में परामर्श के बाद
जब उच्चतम न्यायालय भंग का आदेश देता है
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है प्रधानमंत्री की अनुशंसा पर

Explanation:
भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 85(2)(b) के अनुसार, राष्ट्रपति लोकसभा को उसके कार्यकाल की समाप्ति से पहले ही भंग कर सकते हैं, लेकिन यह शक्ति प्रधानमंत्री की अनुशंसा पर ही प्रयोग की जाती है। यह कार्यपालिका की मंत्रिपरिषद की सलाह पर आधारित है, जो राष्ट्रपति को बाध्य करती है। राष्ट्रपति स्वेच्छा से या उच्चतम न्यायालय के आदेश पर लोकसभा भंग नहीं कर सकते। संसद के संयुक्त सत्र से परामर्श अनिवार्य नहीं है। यह प्रावधान संसदीय प्रणाली का अभिन्न अंग है, जहाँ राष्ट्रपति नाममात्र का प्रमुख होता है और वास्तविक शक्ति प्रधानमंत्री के पास होती है। यदि प्रधानमंत्री विश्वास मत खो देते हैं और वैकल्पिक सरकार नहीं बनती, तब भी अनुशंसा पर ही भंग होता है।

question: Who among the following appoints the Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission of India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Prime Minister
The Chief Justice of India
The President of India
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India

Explanation:
The Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India is appointed by the President of India. This appointment is made on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. The NHRC was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act (1993). The Chairman holds office for a term of 5 years or until he attains the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. The President also has the power to remove the Chairman from office.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who appoints the NHRC Chairman? → The President of India
☛ How many members are in the committee that recommends the NHRC Chairman? → 6 members
☛ Under which act was the NHRC established? → Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
☛ What is the term of the NHRC Chairman? → 5 years or until age 70
☛ Who has the power to remove the NHRC Chairman? → The President of India
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन भारत के राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग के अध्यक्ष की नियुक्ति करता है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3)

भारत के राष्ट्रपति
लोकसभा अध्यक्ष
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत के राष्ट्रपति

Explanation:
भारत के राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग (NHRC) के अध्यक्ष की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है। यह नियुक्ति एक समिति की सिफारिश पर होती है जिसमें प्रधानमंत्री, लोकसभा अध्यक्ष, राज्यसभा के उपसभापति, लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता और राज्यसभा में विपक्ष के नेता शामिल होते हैं। NHRC का गठन मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (1993) के तहत हुआ। अध्यक्ष का कार्यकाल 5 वर्ष या 70 वर्ष की आयु तक, जो भी पहले हो, निर्धारित है। राष्ट्रपति के पास अध्यक्ष को पद से हटाने का भी अधिकार है।

question: Which of the following is NOT a category of judicial review, as classified by Justice Syed Shah Mohammed Quadri? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Judicial review of administrative action of the Union and State and authorities under the state
Judicial review of constitutional amendments
Judicial review of judicial appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts
Judicial review of legislation of the Parliament and State Legislatures and subordinate legislations
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Judicial review of judicial appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts

Explanation:
Justice Syed Shah Mohammed Quadri classified judicial review into three categories: (1) judicial review of administrative action of the Union and State and authorities under the state, (2) judicial review of constitutional amendments, and (3) judicial review of legislation of the Parliament and State Legislatures and subordinate legislations. He did not include judicial review of judicial appointments as a category. Judicial review is an essential feature of the Indian Constitution, empowering the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of actions by the executive and legislature. It upholds the supremacy of the Constitution and ensures a system of checks and balances.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who exercises judicial review in India? → Supreme Court and High Courts
☛ Which article of Indian Constitution deals with the judicial review power of the Supreme Court? → Article 32 and 136
☛ What is the basis of judicial review? → Supremacy of the Constitution
☛ Can constitutional amendments be judicially reviewed? → Yes, under the basic structure doctrine
☛ Which principle is judicial review based on? → Separation of powers

question: Which Act empowered Her Majesty to issue Letters Patent for setting up High Courts? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Charter Act, 1833
Indian High Courts Act, 1861
Regulating Act, 1773
Government of India Act, 1935
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian High Courts Act, 1861

Explanation:
The Indian High Courts Act, 1861 was passed by the British Parliament which empowered Her Majesty to issue Letters Patent for establishing High Courts in India. Under this Act, High Courts were established at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras. This Act was a significant step towards unifying the judicial system in India. It abolished the Supreme Courts and the Sadar Diwani/Faujdari Adalats. The Act also consolidated the legal framework and provided for the administration of justice by High Courts.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was Indian High Courts Act passed? → 1861
☛ Which were the first three High Courts? → Calcutta, Bombay, Madras
☛ Who issued the Letters Patent? → Her Majesty (Queen)
☛ What was the purpose of Indian High Courts Act? → To unify the judicial system
☛ Which courts were abolished by this Act? → Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats

question: Who among the following has the authority to specify an urban area as a 'large urban area' or a 'small urban area' or a 'transitional area' in a state? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: President of India
Chief Justice of the State's High Court
Chief Minister of the State
Governor of the State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor of the State

Explanation:
In India, the authority to specify an urban area as a 'large urban area', 'small urban area', or 'transitional area' lies with the Governor of the State. This provision is under Article 243Q of the Indian Constitution, which deals with the constitution of municipalities. The Governor notifies such classification on the recommendation of the state government. A 'large urban area' has a population of 3 lakh or more, a 'small urban area' has less than 1 lakh, and a 'transitional area' is a region transitioning from rural to urban. This classification is crucial for the formation and administration of urban local bodies.

☛ Small urban area population → Less than 1 lakh
☛ Transitional area → Area transitioning from rural to urban

question: How does the President of India exercise his/her executive functions with respect to decision-making? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: The President considers the advice of the Prime Minister and the Union council of ministers.
The President can repeatedly ask for reconsideration of any ministerial decision until satisfied.
The President acts entirely on his own absolute discretion
The President acts independently of the Union Government for foreign affairs.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President considers the advice of the Prime Minister and the Union council of ministers.

Explanation:
The President of India is the constitutional head of the parliamentary system, but the real executive power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. According to Article 74, the President is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers in the exercise of his/her functions. The President may ask for reconsideration of the advice once, but after reconsideration, he/she is bound to accept it. The President does not act on absolute discretion, nor independently in foreign affairs. This system makes the President a formal head, while the actual power rests with the Council of Ministers.

question: What is the maximum imprisonment term that a Chief Judicial Magistrate can award? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (17/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: 3 years
10 years
Life imprisonment
7 years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 7 years

Explanation:
According to Section 29 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, a Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) can award imprisonment for a maximum term of 7 years. The CJM possesses all the powers of a regular Judicial Magistrate, but with a higher sentencing limit. A regular Judicial Magistrate can award a maximum of 3 years, whereas a CJM can award up to 7 years. This provision empowers the CJM to handle serious offenses, but life imprisonment or death sentence can only be awarded by a Sessions Court or High Court. It is important to note that the CJM cannot award imprisonment exceeding 7 years; any longer term must be imposed by a Sessions Court.

solution:

question: With reference to the 40th Amendment Act, 1976, which category of maritime zones came under the legislative jurisdiction of the Parliament? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Inland rivers and lakes
Inter-state river waters
Groundwater reserves
Territorial waters and EEZ
solution:

Explanation:
The 40th Amendment Act of 1976 added an entry related to maritime zones in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution. This amendment brought territorial waters, continental shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and maritime boundary areas under the legislative jurisdiction of the Parliament. The aim was to bring marine resources and jurisdiction under central control. Inland rivers and lakes fall under the State List, while inter-state river waters and groundwater reserves remain under state jurisdiction. Hence, only territorial waters and EEZ came under Parliament's legislative jurisdiction.

question: Under which List of the Indian Constitution are co-operative societies classified? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Residuary Powers
Concurrent List
State List
Union List
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State List

Explanation:
Under the Indian Constitution, co-operative societies are classified under the State List of the Seventh Schedule. The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 gave constitutional status to co-operative societies. It added Entry 32 to the State List, which deals with the formation, functioning, and regulation of co-operative societies. The amendment also inserted Part IX-B into the Constitution, containing specific provisions for co-operative societies, ensuring democratic functioning and accountability. This amendment aimed to promote co-operative societies and enhance transparency in their management. Thus, co-operative societies fall under the State List, not under the Union List or Concurrent List. The amendment was a significant step to empower the co-operative sector in India.

question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in Part IV of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Promotion of international peace and security
Promotion of Hindi language as a medium of expression
Provision for free and compulsory education for children
Organisation of agricultural and animal husbandry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Promotion of Hindi language as a medium of expression

Explanation:
Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36-51) contains the Directive Principles of State Policy. It includes promotion of international peace and security (Article 51), provision for free and compulsory education for children (Article 45), and organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry (Article 48). Promotion of Hindi language as a medium of expression is NOT mentioned in Part IV; it is part of the Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A). Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

question: Who has the authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: District Collector
Parliament
High Court
State Legislature
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Parliament

Explanation:
Multi-state co-operative societies operate across more than one state, hence their regulation and control require a national framework. According to the Indian Constitution, the authority to make laws for multi-state co-operative societies rests with the Parliament. This power derives from Article 246 and the Concurrent List. The primary legislation governing them is the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002, enacted by Parliament. State legislatures can only legislate on co-operative societies within their respective states. The District Collector and High Court are not law-making bodies; they have executive and judicial roles respectively. This division ensures uniform legal standards for societies operating across state boundaries.

question: Which of the following options best describes the principle of 'collective executive responsibility' as applicable to the Council of Ministers in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: All ministers share full responsibility for government decisions.
Ministers can opt out of collective responsibility if they disagree publicly.
Only the Prime Minister is responsible for decision‑making.
Each minister is independent and is solely accountable for his/her actions.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is All ministers share full responsibility for government decisions.

Explanation:
Under Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means that all ministers bear joint responsibility for every government decision. If a minister disagrees with a decision, he or she can resign but cannot publicly dissent. Collective executive responsibility ensures unity and stability of the government. It is a key feature of the Westminster system where the Council of Ministers acts as a single entity accountable to the Parliament. This principle prevents internal conflicts from undermining the government's functioning.

☛ Can a minister publicly disagree? → No

question: In its advisory capacity, the Union Cabinet’s advice to the President of India is considered: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: overruled by the Speaker of the Lower House
binding to the President
merely suggestive and non-binding
limited only to economic matters
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is binding to the President

Explanation:
According to Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution, there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. This advice is considered binding on the President, as clarified by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976. However, the President can send the advice back for reconsideration, but after reconsideration, it becomes binding. This provision strengthens the parliamentary system of government, where real executive power lies with the Cabinet. The President acts as a constitutional head and follows the Cabinet's advice. This principle is derived from the British constitutional tradition. The binding nature ensures stability and collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What does Article 74(1) primarily state? → The Council of Ministers advises the President, and the advice is binding.
☛ What did the 42nd Amendment 1976 clarify? → The advice of the Council of Ministers is binding on the President.
☛ How many times can the President send advice for reconsideration? → Only once.
☛ Who holds the real executive power? → The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
☛ Which country's constitutional tradition is this system based on? → Britain.

Explanation:

question: Following the provisions of the 74th Constitutional Amendment, 1992, which of the following terms is used for urban governance in areas transitioning from rural to urban? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3)

Nagar Panchayats
Special Economic Zones
Zila Parishads
solution:

Explanation:

It provides for three types of urban bodies: Municipal Corporations for large cities, Municipal Councils for smaller towns, and Nagar Panchayats for areas transitioning from rural to urban. question: When appointing judges to the High Courts, the President of India is required to consult which officials apart from the Chief Justice of India and the Chief Justice of the respective State? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: The State Governor
The local district magistrates
The members of the State Legislature
Only the Union Cabinet
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The State Governor

Explanation:
According to Article 217 of the Indian Constitution, the President appoints judges to the High Courts. In this process, the President must consult the Chief Justice of India, the Chief Justice of the respective State, and the Governor of the State. This consultation is mandatory, though the President is not bound by it. The Governor, as the constitutional head of the state, provides important input regarding the appointment. Other options, such as local district magistrates, members of the State Legislature, or the Union Cabinet, are not part of this consultation process. The Governor's role ensures that the state's perspective is considered in judicial appointments.

Explanation:
The Citizenship Act, 1955 provides four ways to acquire citizenship: by birth, descent, registration, and naturalisation. However, dual citizenship is not allowed under this Act. The Indian Constitution provides for single citizenship. Although the government introduced the Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) scheme in 2005, it does not grant full citizenship rights. OCI holders cannot vote, hold government jobs, or run for political office. Thus, dual citizenship is not legally recognized in India.

☛ Type of citizenship in India → Single citizenship
☛ Full form of OCI → Overseas Citizenship of India
☛ When was OCI introduced → 2005
☛ Right not available to OCI holder → Right to vote

question: In India, judicial review is considered as: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: The power of the judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders
the power of the judiciary to question the wisdom of the executive orders after they are passed by the Union cabinet
the power of the judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President
the power of the judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the legislatures
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The power of the judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders

Explanation:
In India, judicial review refers to the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative laws and executive orders. This power is vested in the Supreme Court and High Courts to ensure that no law or order violates the Constitution. Judicial review is essential for maintaining the supremacy of the Constitution and protecting fundamental rights. It is derived from Articles 13, 32, and 226 of the Indian Constitution. Through judicial review, courts can declare any law or executive action unconstitutional if it infringes upon constitutional provisions. This power acts as a check on the legislature and executive, preventing arbitrary actions and upholding the rule of law.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which article deals with judicial review? → Article 13
☛ Who has the power of judicial review in India? → Supreme Court and High Courts
☛ What is the basis of judicial review? → Supremacy of the Constitution
☛ Which article protects fundamental rights via the Supreme Court? → Article 32
☛ On which principle is judicial review based? → Separation of powers

question: Which Act transferred the power of governance from the East India Company to the British Crown? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Charter Act, 1833
Regulating Act, 1773
Government of India Act, 1858
Pitt’s India Act, 1784
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1858

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1858, ended the rule of the East India Company and transferred the power of governance directly to the British Crown. Under this Act, the British government assumed direct control of India. A new position of Secretary of State for India was created, a member of the British Cabinet, who was responsible for Indian affairs. He was assisted by a Council of India consisting of 15 members. The Governor-General was now called the Viceroy, representing the Crown. This Act was passed in the aftermath of the 1857 Revolt and marked the end of Company rule in India.

☛ Purpose of Government of India Act, 1858 → Transfer rule from East India Company to British Crown
☛ New post created under Government of India Act, 1858 → Secretary of State for India
☛ Number of members in Council of India → 15
☛ New title for Governor-General → Viceroy
☛ Which Act ended Company rule → Government of India Act, 1858
question_hi: किस अधिनियम ने शासन की शक्ति को ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी से ब्रिटिश क्राउन को हस्तांतरित किया? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: चार्टर अधिनियम, 1833
नियमनकारी अधिनियम, 1773
भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1858
पिट का भारत अधिनियम, 1784
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1858

Explanation:
भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1858 (Government of India Act, 1858) ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के शासन को समाप्त कर दिया और शासन की शक्ति सीधे ब्रिटिश क्राउन को हस्तांतरित कर दी। इस अधिनियम के तहत ब्रिटिश सरकार ने भारत का प्रत्यक्ष नियंत्रण ले लिया। एक नए पद भारत के राज्य सचिव (Secretary of State for India) का सृजन किया गया, जो ब्रिटिश कैबिनेट का सदस्य था और भारतीय मामलों का प्रभारी था। उसकी सहायता के लिए 15 सदस्यों वाली भारतीय परिषद (Council of India) बनाई गई। गवर्नर-जनरल को अब वायसराय कहा जाने लगा, जो ब्रिटिश क्राउन का प्रतिनिधि था। यह अधिनियम 1857 के विद्रोह के तुरंत बाद लागू हुआ और इसने कंपनी के शासन के अंत को चिह्नित किया।

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution promotes the spread and development of Hindi? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 350
Article 348
Article 351
Article 349
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 351

Explanation:
Article 351 of the Indian Constitution promotes the spread and development of the Hindi language. It imposes a duty on the Union to promote the spread of Hindi and develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the composite culture of India. It also emphasizes that while developing Hindi vocabulary, words from other Indian languages should be incorporated. This article is part of Part 17 (Official Language). Other options: Article 350 (language for redress of grievances), Article 348 (language in High Courts), and Article 349 (special procedure for language bills).

☛ Article 351 is in which Part → Part 17 (Official Language)

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन सा अनुच्छेद हिंदी के प्रसार और विकास को बढ़ावा देता है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)

अनुच्छेद 351
अनुच्छेद 349
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 351

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 351 हिंदी भाषा के प्रसार और विकास को बढ़ावा देने का प्रावधान करता है। यह अनुच्छेद संघ के कर्तव्य के रूप में कहता है कि सरकार हिंदी के प्रसार को बढ़ावा देगी तथा इसे भारत की समग्र संस्कृति की अभिव्यक्ति का माध्यम बनाने के लिए विकसित करेगी। साथ ही, हिंदी में शब्दावली का निर्माण करते समय अन्य भारतीय भाषाओं के शब्दों को शामिल करने पर जोर दिया गया है। यह अनुच्छेद भाग 17 (राजभाषा) के अंतर्गत आता है। अन्य विकल्पों में अनुच्छेद 350 (शिकायत निवारण में भाषा), अनुच्छेद 348 (उच्च न्यायालयों में भाषा), और अनुच्छेद 349 (भाषा संबंधी विशेष प्रावधान) हैं।
